text.p: National Westminster Bank Plc shares followed the market higher on Wednesday despite downgrades to profit forecasts sparked by Tuesday's results.
The shares put on 5-1/2p to 840-1/2p as the leading FTSE 100 index soared to all-time peaks.

Dealers said BZW cut its full-year forecast to 1.644 billion stg from 1.8 billion and for 1998 to 1.841 billion from two billion. BZW also cut dividend estimates to 32p per share from 33.3p for 1997 and to 36p from 38.2p for 1998. The brokerage house remains a "seller" of the stock.
Top-rated banks analyst Michael Lever at James Capel also cut his figure - to 1.573 billion from 1.72 billion. He was not immediately available to comment on the downgrade.

Earlier the shares dropped to their lowest level - 828p - in a month amid negative press comment on the group's first-half figures. The shares lost 35p on Tuesday after the bank said profits were hit by a slump in its investment banking earnings and ruled out major acquisitions or a merger.
